changes.before: Reject a negative duration while recording cleanup on both success and failure.
changes.after: Use defer to finish cleanup when a function succeeds or throws an error.

before: A throwing function can return a normal result or stop by throwing an error. throws in its signature announces that possibility.
try marks a call that may throw. A do-catch block handles that failure instead of assuming success.
defer schedules work for when the current scope exits, after execution reaches the defer statement. It runs on a normal return or a thrown error.
The supplied Trace is a class containing an events array. Appending a message records the order of operations; caller and function refer to the same trace object.
In checkedMinutes, append "started", register a defer that appends "finished", then reject negative input. Return zero or positive input unchanged.
The supplied inspectMinutes caller records "accepted: N" after success or "rejected" after failure. Cleanup must appear before either caller message.
after: defer schedules work for when the current block ends. It can finish cleanup when a function returns normally or stops by throwing an error.
An error describes a failure. throws says a function may fail. throw stops its normal work and sends an error to the caller. An error type must follow Swift's Error protocol.
try marks a call that may throw. A do-catch block handles that possibility: do holds the attempted work, and catch handles a thrown error.
Zero is too small, so checkedSize throws. Before the function ends, its defer prints Finished. The caller then enters catch. A valid size would also run defer before returning to the caller.
defer only takes effect after the program reaches it. Put it before the work that might fail. It runs when its block ends, not as soon as it is written. It does not turn a failure into a success.
The exercise supplies a Trace object with an events array. Appending text records what happened. The caller and function share this same trace, so both can add events.
In checkedMinutes, append started. Set up defer to append finished. Then throw the supplied error for a negative number. Return zero or a positive number unchanged.

The supplied inspectMinutes caller adds accepted: N after success or rejected after failure. finished must appear before either caller message, because the function's cleanup runs before control returns to the caller.

before.question: A function reaches defer, then throws an error. What happens before the caller's catch runs?
choices: The registered cleanup runs as the function scope exits
Cleanup is skipped because the function did not return normally
defer converts the error into a successful result
before.explanation: A reached defer runs when its scope exits, including by throwing. It does not suppress the error; the caller still handles that error.

after.question: A function reaches defer, then throws. What happens before the caller's catch runs?
choices: defer turns the error into success
after.explanation: The function runs its scheduled cleanup as it exits. The caller then handles the error.

changes.before: defer does not guarantee cleanup after process termination or a scope that never reaches it.
changes.after: defer cannot promise cleanup if the whole process is stopped. It also has no effect when execution never reaches it.
